documents.title: Nurse Visit - Varicella Vaccine Dose 1
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for first varicella dose per PCP order (VZV IgG negative on ID labs 12/17, CD4 220). Denies fever or new illness today. No other live vaccines in the past 4 weeks. Varicella vaccine 0.5 mL subcut left upper arm, VIS given. Told him a mild rash or sore arm can happen within a few weeks; call if a rash shows up. Dose 2 due in 3 months - booked 4/13.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Varicella Vaccine Dose 2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second varicella dose. No reaction after dose 1 other than a sore arm for a day. Feeling well. Got his second COVID shot a few days ago at a community vaccine site; no issue spacing these per protocol. Varicella 0.5 mL subcut right upper arm. Series complete.

documents.title: COVID-19 Vaccine Record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Patient brought in his CDC card. Moderna dose 1 on 3/18/21 and dose 2 on 4/16/21 at the county vaccination clinic. Entered into immunization history; copy scanned.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

Feels good. One year almost without cocaine or meth (last use June 2020); still checks in with his recovery group most weeks. Working steadily on a roofing crew this spring. Still in the transitional program, moved up on the list.

HIV: ID follows, says his last labs there were "good." Takes ART daily, TMP-SMX MWF. Has not needed the fluconazole this year. Both varicella doses done, COVID series done.

ROS negative: no fevers, sweats, cough, mouth sores, diarrhea, rashes, weight change. PHQ-9 2.

Exam: well. HEENT normal, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT, no HSM. Skin: no lesions. Ext: no edema. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. Health maintenance - CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c today (on INSTI-based ART, dad with HTN, mom with T2DM). Tdap 2019, flu yearly, COVID done, varicella series done.
2. HIV - per ID.
3. Polysubstance use disorder - no use in a year. Keep doing what he's doing.
RTC 6 months or prn.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Timothy - labs from your physical look good. Sugar (A1c) normal, cholesterol fine, kidney and liver normal, blood counts normal. Recheck next year.

documents.title: Office Visit - Tongue Lesion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Noticed a white patch on the right side of his tongue about a week ago. Doesn't hurt. Tried his fluconazole for 3 days thinking it was thrush, no change. Also says he's been more tired on and off and his work pants are looser - not trying to lose weight. Hasn't been to ID since the spring; admits he's missed some ART doses this summer.

Exam: weight down a little from June. Oropharynx: whitish patch along the right lateral tongue with a ridged surface; does not come off with a tongue blade. No other oral lesions. No cervical nodes. Lungs clear, heart regular.

A/P
1. Tongue lesion, not removable, no response to fluconazole - not typical thrush. Referral to ENT for evaluation; front desk to request a near-term slot.
2. Fatigue, some weight loss, missed doses - asked him to call ID this week for labs. He agrees.
RTC after ENT.

documents.title: Otolaryngology Consult Letter
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OTOLARYNGOLOGY - CONSULT LETTER
Visit date: 09/01/2021

Thank you for sending this 38-year-old man with HIV. Two weeks of a white area on the side of the tongue, no pain. Some fatigue on and off and weight loss over the last several months. Patient reports more than one current sexual partner and past recreational drug use.

On exam the lesion on the lateral tongue border is corrugated and firmly attached and does not scrape away. No cervical adenopathy.

Impression: oral hairy leukoplakia.

Recommendations: no local treatment needed. It reflects his immune status, so the key step is follow-up with his HIV clinic for viral load, CD4 count and adherence. Happy to see him again if it changes in character.

documents.title: ENT Letter Reviewed
documents.author: RN
documents.body: PCP reviewed ENT letter - oral hairy leukoplakia, no treatment, needs ID follow-up. Called patient. He says he has an ID appointment "in a couple weeks" but didn't know the date. Gave him the ID clinic number again and asked him to confirm it today.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid after work. No contraindications. Asked about COVID booster - plans to get one at the pharmacy next month.

documents.title: COVID-19 Booster Record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: State immunization registry shows Moderna booster given 11/19/21 at a community pharmacy. Added to immunization history.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Tongue plaques still there, now on both sides. Not painful. Bothered by how they look and the texture. He did see ID in the fall; they told him to stick with his ART. He says he's taking it "most days." Weight back up a bit over the holidays. No fevers.

Exam: corrugated white plaques along both lateral tongue borders, unchanged character, do not scrape. No other oral lesions. No nodes. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Oral hairy leukoplakia - persistent. He'd like another opinion about whether anything can be done for the appearance; referral to dermatology (they see oral mucosal lesions). Wait list is long.
2. HIV - adherence again. ID follow-up.
3. Polysubstance use disorder - still no use.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Referral Authorization - Dermatology
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Dermatology office called; MassHealth referral number needed before they can book. Entered referral in the payer portal, number faxed to them. They offered 5/2 at 1:30. Patient notified by text and confirmed.

events.reason: Fatigue, fever, weight loss; oral plaques

documents.title: Dermatology Consult Letter
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY - CONSULT LETTER
Visit date: 05/02/2022

Referred for oral plaques. At the visit his bigger concern was feeling unwell for about two months: tired, fevers off and on, and about 10 kg of weight loss he did not intend. No cough, no diarrhea, no night sweats. Sexually active with more than one partner, does not always use protection. No known drug allergies.

Vitals: T 38.2 C, BP 120/75, HR 88, BMI 21.

Exam: several white, corrugated plaques on the lateral tongue that cannot be wiped off; no other oral lesions. Skin and remainder of exam unremarkable.

Labs drawn here: CD4 180 cells/uL. RPR non-reactive. Hepatitis B surface antigen negative. Hepatitis C antibody negative.

Impression: oral hairy leukoplakia, consistent with the ENT assessment; no dermatologic treatment indicated. The constitutional symptoms and falling CD4 are the more pressing issue and need prompt review by his HIV physician; patient told this directly today. Copy to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after dermatology. Down about 10 kg since February. Tired, fevers on and off. Honest that he's been missing a lot of ART doses since winter - says the pill bottle "gets lost" when he's moving between rooms in the program. No drug use. Eating less, no diarrhea, no cough.

Derm letter reviewed: CD4 180, RPR nonreactive, hep B sAg and hep C Ab negative.

Exam: thin. Afebrile here today. Tongue plaques unchanged. No thrush. No nodes. Lungs clear. Abd soft, no HSM. Skin clear.

A/P
1. HIV with falling CD4, missed doses, weight loss and fevers - needs ID now, not in the fall. Called the ID clinic from the room with him; they will see him next month and draw viral load. Pill organizer given; set a phone alarm together.
2. Weight loss - follow weight. Return in 3 months, sooner if fevers worsen, cough or diarrhea.
3. Oral hairy leukoplakia - unchanged.

documents.title: Follow-up Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called to check whether he made his ID appointment. He went last week, says they "went over everything" and he is back to taking the pill every day with the organizer. No fevers this week. Eating better. Reminded him of August visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Feels better than spring. Fevers stopped. Up 2 kg. Taking ART with the organizer, misses maybe one dose a week. Saw ID in June.

Exam: thin but looks better. Tongue plaques still present, smaller. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
1. HIV - improving adherence; ID follow-up continues.
2. Weight - slowly recovering.
3. Pneumococcal vaccine - indicated with HIV; PCV20 given today, no further pneumococcal doses needed.
4. Flu and COVID bivalent at a nurse visit in October.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine IM left deltoid and Pfizer bivalent COVID booster IM right deltoid. Screening negative. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction.
